candidates.title: DynaVelo predictions identified three genetic rescues tested in mice
candidates.event_date_reason: Nature Biotechnology lists the peer-reviewed version of record as published on 21 October 2026.
candidates.source_date_reason: The publisher gives Published and Version of record as 21 October 2026.
candidates.what_changed: A peer-reviewed Nature Biotechnology paper reported DynaVelo, a neural-ODE model that combines gene expression and transcription-factor motif accessibility. Its in-silico analysis nominated Ctcf, Bcl6 and Stat3 perturbations to rescue an Arid1a-loss phenotype; newly generated double-heterozygous mouse models restored the germinal-center dark-zone/light-zone ratio for all three targets, with deeper multiome comparison for Ctcf.
candidates.why_now: The version of record was published inside the current search window and adds peer-reviewed model, code, data and in-vivo validation evidence beyond the June preprint record.

sources.date_reason: The publisher lists Published and Version of record as 21 October 2026.
sources.relationship_to_sponsor: Peer-reviewed report written by the model developers and experimental collaborators; not an independent replication

sources.date_reason: PMC identifies version 2 of the preprint as posted 23 June 2026.
sources.relationship_to_sponsor: Earlier author manuscript from the same research group; used for method and result locators, not independent corroboration

underlying_identity.cohort: Murine wild-type, Arid1a and Ctcf germinal-center B-cell multiome datasets plus newly generated double-heterozygous mouse models
underlying_identity.product_version: DynaVelo code archived at Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22760121

scope_fit.ai_connection: DynaVelo is a generative neural ordinary differential equation model for single-cell multiomic dynamics and in-silico perturbation.
scope_fit.reader_consequence: Biomedical-model developers get an unusually concrete example of computational perturbation predictions followed by targeted in-vivo tests, while the one-system mouse evidence sets a clear boundary on translational claims.

deduplication.archive_coverage: Title, DynaVelo name, DOI, PMID, preprint DOI and code identity were searched across merged ledgers and stories through contract_ref; no prior HealthTech record was found.

candidates.reason: Select as bounded biomedical-model evidence: the peer-reviewed paper connects in-silico rescue nominations to newly generated mouse models and releases code and data, while the story will avoid therapy, patient-benefit and general biological-causality claims.

evidence.publication_status: Peer-reviewed open-access Nature Biotechnology version of record published 21 October 2026; earlier preprint posted 23 June 2026.
evidence.study_design: Computational method development and evaluation on single-cell RNA and chromatin-accessibility data, followed by targeted genetic perturbation experiments in mice.
evidence.validation_setting: Wild-type and mutant murine germinal-center B cells; new compound-heterozygous mouse models tested Ctcf, Bcl6 and Stat3 rescue nominations, with single-cell multiome profiling for the Ctcf double mutant.
evidence.independent_validation: No independent replication was found. The biological experiments were performed by the same author group, although the Bcl6 and Stat3 mouse models were newly generated after model nomination.
evidence.funding: The funding declaration did not surface in the inspected publisher extract and is recorded as unavailable; no funding source is inferred.
evidence.conflicts_of_interest: The competing-interest declaration did not surface in the inspected publisher extract and is recorded as unavailable; absence of an extracted declaration is not evidence of no conflict.
evidence.corrections_retractions: No correction, retraction or withdrawal notice was identified on the publisher record or PubMed/PMC records during the 23 October 2026 check.
contradictory_findings: The paper reports that predicted motif-velocity changes agreed better than RNA-velocity changes and that rescue magnitudes varied across cell types and modalities, limiting any claim of uniform predictive accuracy.
limitations: The work evaluates one murine germinal-center B-cell system and heterozygous genetic perturbations; it does not establish performance in human tissue, other cell systems or disease treatment.
The same author group developed the model and conducted the validation experiments; no external replication was identified.
Restoration of a dark-zone/light-zone ratio is a preclinical phenotype, not evidence of therapeutic benefit, safety or patient outcome.

The model uses inferred RNA velocity and transcription-factor motif accessibility from destructive single-time-point measurements, so its dynamics are model-dependent rather than direct longitudinal observations.
The paper reports more complete multiomic validation for Ctcf than for Bcl6 and Stat3, whose confirmation centers on immunophenotypic ratio rescue.
evidence.applicability: Relevant to computational biologists designing perturbation models and validation plans. It supports experimentally testing model-nominated interactions in matched systems, not selecting a human therapeutic target.

claims.supported_statement: In one murine germinal-center B-cell system, DynaVelo nominated Ctcf, Bcl6 and Stat3 perturbations as rescues for an Arid1a-loss phenotype; compound-heterozygous mouse experiments restored the dark-zone/light-zone ratio toward wild type for all three, with multiome profiling additionally showing partial recovery across four modalities for Ctcf.
locators: Nature Biotechnology abstract, Results section 'In silico perturbations of Arid1a mutant GCs identify candidate targets for rescuing the loss of function', Figure 6 and Discussion.
PMC full text lines 237-266 and Figure 6 legend: nomination, sample counts, ratio rescue and Ctcf modality-specific rescue rates.
claims.evidence_scope: Same-team computational and in-vivo validation in genetically engineered mice; no claim about human disease, therapy, patient benefit or general performance across biological systems.
limitations: The three targets share one biological system and phenotype; deeper multiomic validation was reported for Ctcf only.
Model-derived velocities and inferred latent dynamics are not direct time-series measurements.

verification.checked_by: ChatGPT GPT-6 (model source review; not independent human or biological validation)
verification.supported_scope: The peer-reviewed version of record and accessible author manuscript directly support the identities of all three nominated perturbations, the new Bcl6 and Stat3 mouse models, restoration of the dark-zone/light-zone ratio and modality-specific Ctcf rescue measurements.
verification.reason: The claim was narrowed to the tested murine system and phenotype, distinguishes same-team validation from independent replication and excludes therapeutic or patient-benefit language.

study.design: Neural-ODE model development and retrospective prediction on paired single-cell RNA and chromatin-accessibility data, followed by prospective targeted creation and immunophenotyping of compound-heterozygous mouse models.
study.setting: Murine germinal-center B cells under wild-type, Arid1a and Ctcf genetic conditions.
study.population_or_dataset: Seven initial multiome samples plus six new multiome validation samples; separate newly generated Arid1aHet;Bcl6Het and Arid1aHet;Stat3Het mouse cohorts for phenotype tests.

sample_sizes.unit: mouse samples across Bcl6 and Stat3 rescue experiments
sample_sizes.reason: Figure 6 legend reports 24 samples in the Bcl6 experiment and 30 in the Stat3 experiment.
Data-availability statement reports two wild-type, two Arid1aHet and two Arid1aHet;CtcfHet samples.

study.comparator: Wild-type, single-heterozygous and compound-heterozygous germinal-center phenotypes; predicted velocity shifts were compared with observed mutant and rescue profiles.
primary_endpoints: Agreement of predicted perturbation effects with observed differential RNA and motif velocities.
Restoration of the germinal-center dark-zone/light-zone ratio in compound-heterozygous mice.
secondary_exploratory_endpoints: Recovery of RNA expression, RNA velocity, motif accessibility and motif velocity toward wild-type values in the Ctcf double mutant.

results.value: restored to wild-type levels in both compound-heterozygous backgrounds
results.uncertainty: Exact effect sizes and confidence intervals did not surface in the inspected text; sample groups were WT 6, Arid1aHet 6, Bcl6Het 6, DKO 6 and WT 10, Arid1aHet 10, Stat3Het 6, DKO 4.

results.endpoint: Ctcf rescue across modalities in the most disrupted CC cell type
results.metric: Features shifted from Arid1aHet toward wild type
results.value: 38% RNA expression; 64% RNA velocity; 51% motif accessibility; 46% motif velocity
results.comparator: Arid1aHet versus Arid1aHet;CtcfHet and wild-type profiles
results.uncertainty: Reported as modality-specific rescue fractions in the same-team validation; not an external confidence interval or patient outcome.

study.follow_up: Endpoint-specific mouse experiments; no clinical or longitudinal patient follow-up.
study.harms: No therapeutic safety or animal-harm outcome was reported as an efficacy endpoint in the inspected sections.
study.analysis_notes: The study also reports incomplete agreement between predicted and observed velocity changes; motif velocities performed better than RNA velocities. Rescue of one phenotype does not validate every predicted network edge.
study.applicability: Supports a workflow in which in-silico perturbation nominations are subjected to matched biological experiments; generalization outside the studied murine system is untested.

rationales.significance: The link from model nomination to newly generated in-vivo tests is consequential for biomedical-model evaluation, but the evidence remains preclinical and system-specific.
rationales.claim_support: Peer-reviewed full-text excerpts, released code/data and mouse experiments support the bounded claim; missing extracted funding/COI declarations and no independent replication cap support.
rationales.relevance: Directly relevant to biomedical AI and computational-biology readers, though less immediate for clinical operations.
rationales.material_change: The 21 October peer-reviewed version of record packages the model, artifacts and biological validation as a new confirmed publication.
rationales.durability: The validation pattern and released artifacts should remain useful beyond the news cycle, while specific biological findings still need broader replication.

publication_verification.checked_by: ChatGPT GPT-6 (model source review; not independent human or biological validation)
publication_verification.supported_scope: The live Nature Biotechnology record confirms the 21 October version of record, model and code/data availability, the three target nominations and same-team mouse validation. The accessible manuscript supports detailed result locators and reported sample counts.
publication_verification.reason: Fresh inspection found no correction or retraction and supports a specialist briefing limited to preclinical model validation in one mouse system.

decision_history.reason: Cleared the 75-point gate with peer-reviewed, directly inspectable preclinical validation and explicit translational limits.
